summary: Exact candidate 378ebac401a21abfa048a3880426bdb995ccabc4 is a valid narrow fix for the original issue's Llama32 streaming JSON-string corruption item. The recorded base corrupts or drops calls containing the reported single-quote patterns; the candidate preserves them across complete and adversarially split increments and retains Python-dict compatibility. It is a partial fix because the original issue enumerates multiple independent detector defects that this commit does not change.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction against the real Llama32Detector. Both reported quote patterns and related JSON-string cases were corrupted; the Python single-quoted-dict compatibility control passed.
Candidate regression suite: 10 Llama32 tests passed, including both reported corruption patterns, a cross-chunk case, and preservation of Python single-quoted-dict conversion.

Independent adversarial round-trip cases passed for complete input and boundaries before/inside/after vulnerable patterns, escaped double quotes, backslashes, Unicode, multiple patterns, and the existing Python-dict compatibility behavior.
Complete shared function-call parser module: 246 tests passed with 4 subtests; only the existing unknown asyncio_mode configuration warning was emitted.

gpu_execution.evidence: An AMD Instinct MI350X was visible, but the reviewed defect is deterministic CPU string parsing after detokenization. No model weights, HTTP serving, semantic accuracy, distributed execution, or GPU result is claimed.

remaining_counterexamples: base_format_detector name-send branch can lose arguments or parallel calls
Step3 parameter matching can cross an invoke boundary and graft/drop calls
KimiK2 can fail to retain a lone trailing '<' token prefix
KimiK2 can stream a split end-token prefix into arguments
DeepSeekV3 greedy streaming matching can assign the second call's name to the first
DeepSeekV3/V31 can discard already-valid calls when a later call is malformed
Base/Mistral normal-text cleanup can delete ordinary ']' characters
Llama32 non-streaming separator accounting can drop the first trailing-text character
Pythonic detector bracket matching can mis-slice brackets inside string literals
remaining_limitations: This review validates one Llama32 parser defect, not the full multi-detector original issue.
No full model, HTTP serving path, model semantics, multi-node workload, or GPU kernel was exercised; none is required to reproduce this decoded-text parser bug.
No native code changed, so a native rebuild was neither applicable nor performed.
The candidate's Python-literal fallback remains intentionally narrow and was not qualified for every possible Python literal or escaped single-quoted string form.
